name: Redline

idea.pitch: An AI that reads the contract before you sign it

jobs.when: a client sends me a contract
jobs.want: to know which clauses could hurt me
jobs.so: I don’t sign something that costs me money
I can push back without a lawyer

jobs.want: an email that’s firm but friendly

jobs.when: I sign a lot of contracts
jobs.want: to see what I agreed to before

jobs.when: the contract arrives as a PDF
jobs.want: to drop it in as it is
jobs.so: I don’t have to copy text

jobs.want: my team to use it too
jobs.so: we all sign on the same terms

pays.who: Alex, a freelance designer with a new client
pays.why: One bad clause costs more than a check. Today it is £400 for a lawyer, or an evening of worry.

argued.reason: There is nothing to check without it
Without trade and country the flags are generic, and wrong
It is the reason anyone pays
It is how the job gets paid for
The journey’s last step needs it
The wording is the hard part; Alex can write the email
Pay per contract, no login needed

journey.text: Reads the red flags, worst first, and why each matters
Copies what to ask for instead, for each flag

stories.text: As a freelancer, I want to open Redline and see where to paste, so that I can start without signing up.
stories.done: The first screen has the paste box and nothing else to fill in.

stories.text: As a freelancer, I want to paste a contract’s text, so that I can check it without uploading files.
As a freelancer, I want to give my trade and country, so that the flags fit my work and my law.
stories.done: Both are used in the check and shown on the report.

stories.text: As a freelancer, I want to pay for just this contract, so that I don’t need a subscription.
stories.done: The report opens only after payment.

stories.text: As a freelancer, I want the risky clauses ranked worst first with a plain-English why, so that I know what matters.
stories.done: Each flag quotes its clause and says why; the report says it isn’t legal advice.

stories.text: As a freelancer, I want wording to ask for instead of each flag, so that I can push back without a lawyer.
stories.done: Every flag has a replacement clause to copy.

testCases: Three sample contracts, one of them nasty

unknowns.test: Put a payment link in front of 10 freelancers. Do 3 pay?

unknowns.text: Pasting text is fine; PDFs can wait.
unknowns.test: Count how many people give up at the paste step.

unknowns.text: A plain-English why is enough to act on, without a lawyer.
unknowns.test: After the report, ask: would you send a pushback based on this?

unknowns.text: Freelancers want the pushback email more than accounts.
unknowns.test: Ask the first ten paying users which they would pay for next.

log.q: Say the idea in one breath. Who is it for?
log.a: An AI that reads the contract before you sign it, for freelancers.

log.q: When does Alex need this, and what does it get them?
log.a: When a client sends a contract, so they don’t sign something that costs money.

log.q: Who would pay to have this done, today? Name them.
log.a: Alex, a freelance designer quoted £400 by a lawyer for a 20-page contract.

log.q: How much would Alex pay, per contract?
log.a: About £9 a contract, less than an hour of a lawyer.

log.q: What does the product do, under each job?
log.a: Thirteen features across the six jobs.

log.q: Walk me through J1, from the first thing Alex does.
log.a: Six steps, from opening Redline to copying what to ask for.

log.q: They’ve read the red flags. And then what happens?
log.a: They need to know what to ask for instead. That is where the job’s “so” is reached.

log.q: Which features does the journey need? Everything else, which column?
log.a: The room’s first draft: the AI can do it all anyway.

log.q: That makes 11 pieces. Does that count look right to you?
log.a: Yes, 11.

log.q: Walk it as Alex, touching only stage 1. Where do you get stuck?
log.a: Step 6: the report says what’s wrong, not what to ask for. Add F5 from J2.

log.q: Would Alex still pay without accounts?
log.a: Yes: pay per contract, no login needed.

log.q: Would Alex still pay without PDF upload?
log.a: Yes: pasting the text works.

log.q: Would Alex still pay without the pushback email?
log.a: Yes: the wording is the hard part; Alex can write the email.

log.q: Would Alex still pay without trade and country?
log.a: No: without them the flags are generic, and wrong.

log.q: Would Alex still pay without the red-flag report?
log.a: No. It is the reason anyone pays.

log.q: For each step: what would Alex see if it works?
log.a: Five stories, in journey order.

log.q: Which contracts will you test with after every change?
log.a: Three sample contracts, one of them nasty.

log.q: Five features, six pieces. Small enough to build in a day?
log.a: Yes.

log.q: Everything outside stage 1, in pencil: which features does each later one need first?
log.a: Compare and standard terms need accounts; the rest stand on stage 1.

log.q: Which of these would freelancers pay for next?
log.a: Push back: the pushback email is what they asked for most.
